full_judgment: 9. Mr Md Nawab Ali, the learned Advocate-on- Record appearing on behalf of the appellants submitted that for the selfsame occurrence the appellants were tried for offences under sections 7/8/30 of the Ain, 2000 and the appellant Nos. l and 2 were convicted by the Tribunal by the judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 30-4-2003 and sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for life. The appellant No.3 was acquitted from the charge levelled against him. He submitted that the High Court Division, therefore, erred in allowing continuation of the proceedings under sections 302/2011/34 of the Penal Code which arose out of the self-same occurrence. He also submitted that the appellants would thereby be subjected to double jeopardy if they are made to suffer the trial again for the death and dis- appearance of the same victim, for which they have already been tried, convicted and sentenced. He finally submitted that the Tribunal had the power to try the offences under sections 302/201/34 of the Penal Code simultaneously as provided by section 27(3) of the Ain, 2000. That having not been done, the second trial over the same occurrence by the Court of Sessions is barred under Article 35 of the Constitution.
